prompt: A company must create identical environments in several Regions and wants to avoid manual mistakes. What should it use?

options.explanation: Correct. Templates make deployments repeatable and consistent.

options.text: Manual steps in the AWS Management Console
options.explanation: Manual steps can leave environments inconsistent.
AWS Artifact provides compliance documents.
AWS Budgets tracks costs.

explanation: Repeatable environments point to infrastructure as code.

prompt: A company keeps some systems in its own data center and connects them to workloads running on AWS. Which deployment model is this?

options.explanation: Correct. A hybrid model connects cloud resources to on-premises infrastructure.
A cloud model runs fully in the cloud.
An on-premises model does not use the cloud in this way.
SaaS is a service model, not a deployment model.

explanation: Cloud connected to on-premises is hybrid.

prompt: A developer wants an application written in Python to call AWS services directly. Which option should the developer use?

options.explanation: Correct. SDKs let applications call AWS from programming languages.
The console is a web interface for people.
Direct Connect is a network connection.
Trusted Advisor recommends improvements.

explanation: Calling AWS from application code points to an SDK.

references.title: AWS SDKs and Tools Reference Guide

prompt: A new employee wants to explore a service once to see how it works. Which option is most suitable?

options.explanation: Correct. The console suits learning and one-off tasks.
Templates are valuable for repeatable work, which this is not.

options.text: A custom application built with an SDK
options.explanation: This is far more work than a one-off look needs.
Outposts runs AWS infrastructure on site.

prompt: A company needs to run AWS infrastructure inside its own building. Which service provides this?

options.explanation: Correct. AWS Outposts runs AWS infrastructure at a customer site.
Lightsail is a simple way to run small applications on AWS.
CloudFront delivers content through edge locations.
CloudFormation provisions resources from templates.

explanation: AWS infrastructure at your own site points to AWS Outposts.
